description:
Audit a Markdown research/proof workspace before deciding current progress or next propositions.

Use this as a compact map of verified results, knowledge notes, underexposed proof conclusions, verified infrastructure, and possible blocker/assembly language. Treat the result as navigation evidence, not as a deterministic verdict: read the cited files before relying on a claim, and compare it with research_reviewer reports when both are available. If the result includes a suggested next proposition with a selected target, inspect that target before broadening; if you choose a different research direction, state what evidence makes the selected target irrelevant, already statement-visible, or lower priority. If the selected target is choice-classification, do not rank conditional assembly or stronger machinery first unless the choice scan is already complete or irrelevant by cited evidence. If the selected target is an underclaimed answer-facing bound/value/threshold/stopping condition, do not rank it below speculative harder routes. A Statement gap that changes the original problem's visible bound, value, stopping condition, or theorem interface is not ordinary bookkeeping merely because harder downstream work remains.
name: ResearchProgressReview

path.description: Workspace root or directory to audit. Use `.` for the current research workspace.

paths.description: Optional specific files/directories to scan instead of auto-detecting research folders.

description:
Inspect Markdown files or narrow directories by surfacing headings, statement/progress sections, and proof tails.

Use this after ResearchProgressReview, Grep, or a reviewer report cites specific files whose statements, proof endings, or progress notes matter for the next research decision.
name: InspectMarkdown

max_files.description: Maximum Markdown files to inspect when path is a directory.

path.description: Markdown file or directory to inspect.

statement_lines.description: Maximum lines to show from each selected statement/progress section.

tail_lines.description: How many ending lines to show for each file.

description:
Searches readable text files under a specific file or directory.

Usage:
- Prefer Grep for exact symbol/string searches before reading many files.
- Narrow `path` when you know the likely directory; broad searches can hit the result limit quickly.
- Returns plain text in `path:line: text` format, optionally with context.
- Use `context_lines` when the surrounding lines matter; keep it small for compact output.
- `regex` defaults to true; set `regex=false` to force plain substring matching.
- Results respect this agent's workspace access restrictions.
name: Grep

context_lines.description: Number of context lines around each match.

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to this agent's configured search root.

pattern.description: The text or regular expression pattern to search for in file contents.

regex.description: Treat pattern as a regex (default: true; set false for substring matching).

description: Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size. Supports glob patterns like ``**/*.md`` or ``src/**/*.py``, or ``*`` to list directory contents.
name: Glob

path.description: The directory to search in. Defaults to this agent's configured search root.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against.

description:
Read text content from a file.

Tips:
- In AlphaSolve research workspaces, this is an exact file-inspection tool, not the primary way to survey progress across many propositions or notes.
- For broad progress review over `problem.md`, `verified_propositions/`, and `knowledge/`, run ResearchProgressReview first; then use Read on the cited files that need line-level precision.
- A `<system>` tag will be given before the read file content.
- The system will notify you when there is anything wrong when reading the file.
- This tool is worth using in parallel only after a progress map or explicit citation has narrowed the files to inspect.
- For Markdown proposition files with Statement and Proof sections, the default call with only `path` returns the Statement section plus the file tail; set `read_all=true` or pass `line_offset`/`n_lines` for exact proof inspection.
- If you want to search for a certain content or pattern, prefer Grep over Read.
- Content will be returned with a line number before each line like `cat -n` format.
- By default, Read returns 250 lines.
- `line_offset` is the first line to return.
- `n_lines` is how many lines to return in this call; default is 250.
- Set `read_all=true` to ignore `n_lines` and read from `line_offset` to the end of the file.
- Without `read_all`, the maximum `n_lines` value is 1000.
- Results respect this agent's workspace access restrictions.
- For multi-file research progress review, prefer `ResearchProgressReview` before broad manual reading. Use `Read` after the progress map has identified specific files or when a single cited file needs exact line-level inspection.
- If a Read result reports a proposition-index gap or an underclaimed proof tail, resolve whether that already-established conclusion should be surfaced before continuing broad exploration.
name: Read

line_offset.description: The line number to start reading from. By default read from the beginning of the file. Set this when the file is too large to read at once.

n_lines.description: How many lines to return in this Read call. Defaults to 250. At most 1000 unless `read_all` is true.

path.description: The path to the file to read (must be absolute or workspace-relative).

read_all.description: If true, ignore n_lines and return every line from line_offset through the end of the file.

description:
Writes a file within this agent's allowed write area.

Usage:
- Use `mode="overwrite"` to replace the whole file.
- Use `mode="append"` to append content to the end of the file.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents.
- Treat index writes as objective bookkeeping after the research target is clear. Use SyncResearchState rather than Write for strategic state.md.
name: Write

content.description: The content to write to the file.

mode.description: Whether to overwrite the whole file or append to the end.

path.description: The path to the file to write.

description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- The edit will FAIL if old_string is not unique in the file.
- Provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique.
- Treat index edits as objective bookkeeping after the research target is clear. Use SyncResearchState rather than Edit for strategic state.md.
name: Edit

new_str.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string).

path.description: The path to the file to modify.

description:
Lists files and directories under a workspace directory.

Usage:
- Returns plain text with one entry per line; directories end with `/`.
- If the directory contains `index.md`, read `index.md` first before exploring other files.
- The result respects this agent's workspace access restrictions.
- If a research workspace contains both `verified_propositions/` and `knowledge/`, use `ResearchProgressReview` as the progress map before manually reading many index or proposition files.
name: ListDir

path.description: Directory to list. Defaults to this agent's configured read root.

description: Creates a directory within the writable workspace area, including parent directories when needed.
name: MakeDir

description:
Renames a file or directory in place within the writable workspace area.

Usage:
- Use this only when the item stays in the same directory and only its name changes.
- `directory` is the parent directory that currently contains the item.
- `old_name` and `new_name` must be plain names, not paths, and must not contain `/` or `\`.
- To move a file into another directory, use Move instead.
- You may rename verified proposition Markdown files inside `verified_propositions/` and any of its subdirectories.
- If two verified propositions have the same filename, use Rename to give one proposition a more specific name and prevent conflicts.
- When renaming Markdown files inside `verified_propositions/`, Rename automatically updates matching `\ref{old-path}` references across verified propositions to the new backslash-separated path.
- This tool fails if the target path already exists.

Examples:
- Rename a folder: directory="verified_propositions", old_name="graph-route", new_name="graph-coloring-route".
- Rename a verified proposition file: directory="verified_propositions/graph-route", old_name="cycle-bound.md", new_name="odd-cycle-coloring-obstruction-bound.md".
name: Rename

directory.description: Parent directory containing the item to rename.

new_name.description: New file or directory name only; no path separators.

old_name.description: Current file or directory name only; no path separators.

description:
Moves a file into another directory within the writable workspace area while keeping the same file name.

Usage:
- Use this when reorganizing files into topic folders.
- `path` must be an existing file.
- `destination_dir` must be an existing directory.
- Move never renames the file; it always keeps the source file name.
- When moving files inside verified_propositions/, Move automatically updates matching `\ref{old-path}` references across verified_propositions/ to the new backslash-separated path.
name: Move

description:
Start one worker and return immediately; this tool does not wait for the worker to finish.

Worker lifecycle:
- The worker first runs generator to draft one candidate proposition.
- It then runs verifier; if verification fails and rounds remain, it runs reviser and repeats verifier -> reviser.
- After verification, theorem-checking decides whether the verified proposition resolves the original problem.

Return content is JSON containing whether a worker was spawned, plus active_count, active_worker_ids, active_workers, max_workers, and available_worker_slots. If the parallelism limit has been reached, call TaskOutput before spawning more workers.
name: SpawnWorker

blocker_override_reason.description: Required only when this direction has an active process-audit blocker and this spawn targets a different gap. State the concrete new evidence that justifies pivoting instead of directly attacking that blocker.

consolidation.description: Optional (default false). Set true to spawn a CONSOLIDATION / DUAL attempt on a FIXED target: the worker may NOT weaken the statement, narrow it, add fresh hypotheses, or isolate a smaller sub-claim to pass verification. Only two results count as success: proving the pinned target exactly as stated, or refuting it with an explicit checkable witness (construction/counterexample). Use this to (a) cash out a direction whose verified props have accumulated, by attacking its terminal goal head-on, or (b) run the dual/falsification of a persistently-failing target. Pass the target text via pinned_target and give the direction's mainline props via frontier_refs.

difficulty_id.description: Canonical curator-owned difficulty ID. Prefer an executable leaf returned by DifficultyFrontier, but an internal parent may be selected when its exact obligation is more informative. The runtime returns a leaf-first warning with active child IDs rather than rejecting that deliberate choice.

frontier_note.description: Optional. One short note telling the worker what the curated frontier means for this hint or what to avoid (e.g. 'avoid the anchor-graph mainline; try construction/number-theoretic structure such as 45^2'). Shown alongside frontier_refs.

frontier_refs.description: Optional. A curated list of verified-proposition references (paths relative to `verified_propositions` without the `.md` extension, subdirectories with backslashes, e.g. `structural\anchor-graph\anchor-graph-for-rectangle-partition`) that define the research frontier this worker should build on. The runtime injects each referenced proposition's Statement into the worker's task so the worker can focus on its assigned mathematical obligation instead of broad workspace exploration. Differentiate this per direction: give an exploit spawn its mainline frontier, give a new/orthogonal direction a small orthogonal set, and leave it empty for a free-exploration direction that should start from scratch.

global_attack.description: Optional (default false). Set true to launch a GLOBAL consolidation that attacks `problem.md` directly — not any canonical difficulty leaf. This implies consolidation=true (no weakening allowed). Read DifficultyFrontier.global_consolidation_directive first: the runtime permits the first attack and each later attack only after the configured number of verified propositions has accumulated; a completed attack resets that count. Every completed global attack is reported to the curator for knowledge and later DAG curation. If pinned_target is omitted, the runtime reads problem.md into pinned_target automatically. Do NOT pass difficulty_id with global_attack.

hint.description: Optional targeted hint for this worker only. Suggest a direction, method, branch, local target, or auxiliary assumption. This is different from the user's hint.md.

method_id.description: Optional proof/search method for the selected difficulty leaf.

parent_direct_attack.description: Optional (default false). Mark a fixed-target attack on an internal parent returned by DifficultyFrontier.parent_direct_difficulties. The runtime pins the exact parent statement, records the attempt against its recommended interval, and returns a warning if that interval is not replenished.

parent_id.description: Backward-compatible single parent attempt state_id. These describe attempt lineage only; they do not modify the difficulty DAG.

parent_ids.description: Optional parent attempt state_ids for the attempt DAG. Pass multiple ids for crossover. These describe lineage only; the canonical difficulty_id identifies the mathematical obligation.

pinned_target.description: Optional. The exact target statement to attack when consolidation=true. If omitted, the worker uses the goal expressed in `hint`. Ignored when consolidation is false.

rubric.description:
Optional. A concise acceptance checklist (3-6 bullet points, each starting with '- ') specifying what the proven Statement must satisfy to count as progress on the assigned difficulty. The rubric is NOT shown to the worker — it is stored and returned to you in TaskOutput for evidence-based assessment via RecordDifficultyOutcome. Example: '- Explicit construction of a permutation and tiling
- Rectangle count k <= 2111
- All non-hole cells covered exactly once'. Write criteria that are checkable against the proven Statement alone.

description:
Launch a new specialized agent and return its final report.

The launched agent runs in a separate session. It does not see this conversation unless you include the needed context in `prompt`.

Available agent types:
- compute_subagent: Concrete symbolic or numeric computation and verification.
- curator: Incrementally update the knowledge wiki from local traces and synthesize portfolio checkpoints by comparing worker outcomes and process audits.
- numerical_experiment_subagent: Bounded exploration, branch checks, local numerical experiments, small-n exhaustive search, counterexample mining, invariant discovery, and constraint-gap quantification. Use when analytic progress is blocked and a numerical probe could reveal which unproven lemma is most likely to close the gap. Can run exhaustive enumeration, LP formulations, and structural invariant extraction on small-n analogues.

- reasoning_subagent: Bounded proof and mathematical reasoning obligations.
- research_reviewer: After a cold-start worker batch or later evidence collection, compare verified propositions, worker results, handoffs, and the canonical frontier; identify one next obligation, adversarially review it once, and perform at most one decision-critical bounded numerical check.

## Writing the prompt

- For broad workspace review, split by directory or file group: ask each subagent to inspect one scoped area and return a concise evidence report with file paths, line references when available, current status, open issues, and recommended next local step.
- Use the main agent to compare subagent reports and decide the global next step; do not ask a subagent with a narrow scope to make the final workspace-wide decision.
- State the exact claim, definitions, assumptions, and what needs to be proved or checked.
- Include relevant context: what's already known, what approaches have been tried, which files to reference, and why this task matters.
- Give enough context that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- Keep the task self-contained and limited to the agent's scope.
- `research_reviewer` returns a single research plan, not a list to pick from. It has its own scoped `Agent` tool (restricted to `reasoning_subagent`/`numerical_experiment_subagent`) and must return both an "Adversarial Review" and a `Route Validation` section. `VERDICT: CLEAR` only means the plan survived critique; before dispatch, obey `Route Validation`'s `DISPATCH:` status. For `BLOCKED` or `NEEDS_FALSIFICATION`, record the supplied evidence with `RecordDispatchConstraint`; only `READY_FOR_PROOF` permits a normal proof worker. This remains a prompt-level report, so check that its cited numerical coverage and counterexample search are substantive before trusting it.
- When using `research_reviewer`, delegate an independent progress audit rather than a proof attempt for the route you currently favor.
- Include any already-seen proposition-index gaps or underclaimed proof-tail evidence in the prompt, especially any `ResearchProgressReview` suggested next proposition and selected target, and ask the reviewer to rank that candidate against broader theorem work.
- If underclaimed proof-tail evidence only quantifies why one conditional route is obstructed, and the problem still asks for an existential choice among models, parameters, data, weights, or ansatzes, ask the reviewer to use that obstruction as a constraint on the choice-classification target rather than replacing the constructive scan.
- If underclaimed proof-tail evidence changes a numerical bound, objective value, threshold, stopping condition, or answer-facing inequality, do not demote explicit Statement consolidation below speculative research directions unless another verified Statement already records it.
- When the workspace has many verified local estimates for one shared energy, bootstrap, reduction, or interface system, ask whether the next proposition should assemble the exact system levels, constants, remainders, and restrictions before attacking another local lemma.
- If a local repair appears to be one component of a larger system interface, ask the reviewer whether the durable next proposition should be the exact interface with that repair listed as a premise, rather than the repair in isolation.
- If downstream propositions look ready to promote but rely on a support, domain, time-scale, interface, or parameter-choice prerequisite that is still conditional, slackened, or not Statement-visible, ask the reviewer to rank that prerequisite before the downstream promotion unless the prerequisite is already established in verified_propositions.
- If the problem asks for existence of a model, parameter regime, input family, weight, or ansatz, and the workspace already has a conditional theorem chain, ask the reviewer whether the next proposition should classify choices that make the existing chain's hypotheses hold before inventing stronger general estimates.
- A choice-classification target should cover the whole theorem interface, including support/domain conditions, lower-bound or positivity hypotheses, nonlinear remainder control, regularity/smallness assumptions, and the timescale on which the resulting inequality must hold.
- Do not let a framework-formalization, conditional assembly, or gap-naming task outrank a choice-classification task when it would only restate that some model, parameter, data, weight, or ansatz choice must satisfy the existing chain's hypotheses.
- Do not replace that scan with re-proving verified infrastructure, sharper constants, alternative test functions, or stronger PDE/ODE machinery unless the choice-classification scan is already complete or rules out viable choices.
- When a verified proposition Statement conflicts with an index or knowledge summary, treat the verified Statement as authoritative and ask whether the summary is stale rather than planning from the weaker summary.
- If a reviewed `unverified_propositions/` file already has a passed review and records a system interface, constants, derivative levels, assumptions, or obstruction, ask whether promoting or repairing that proposition is the best verified-progress step before opening a new local route.
- `research_reviewer` now returns one primary plan (plus ≤2 one-line rejected alternatives), not a ranked list — treat that plan as a prior, not a command. Each `selection_advice` from `TaskOutput` carries a read-only `frontier` list ranking active worker nodes by cheap proxy signals (open subgoals, verified implications, falsification hits) — nothing is pre-selected for you. If the reviewer's plan targets a direction whose recent workers only produced necessary_condition_only/orthogonal outputs, while `frontier` shows another direction with stronger verified implications and no falsification hits, prefer the latter. The reviewer's plan reflects a static workspace snapshot; `frontier` reflects what workers actually achieved. Update your belief accordingly.
- If the reviewer's plan is an exact system or interface assembly, do not demote it as bookkeeping merely because it may expose a harder local gap; that assembly may be the research proposition needed to determine which local gap is actually blocking the proof.
- Do not present an unverified route as the core blocker unless a verified proposition, knowledge synthesis, or prior reviewer report explicitly identifies it as such.
- Whether `research_reviewer` reads `verified_propositions/**/state.md` (your prior strategic notes) is decided automatically by the system via an epsilon-greedy policy and recorded in the run log. You do not need to set `read_state` for `research_reviewer` — the system assigns it and overrides any value you pass.
name: Agent

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform.

read_state.description: Optional; only meaningful for research_reviewer. If true, the reviewer may consult verified_propositions/**/state.md (prior strategic notes). If false or omitted, the reviewer forms an independent assessment and does not read state.md, avoiding being steered by a previous wrong route.

type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task.

description:
Start one worker for open-ended, non-targeted exploration and return immediately (does not wait). You may use this while canonical leaves exist, but must supply a concrete reason why an orthogonal route is worth a worker slot. The runtime records that frontier deviation, the available canonical leaves, and the worker's eventual outcome. It still refuses this tool while a completed process audit needs curator blocker classification.

The worker receives persisted failed-method taboos, active repeated blockers, and an optional under-explored verified seed. It must choose a distinct bounded claim or record why no such claim is available. Returns the same shape as SpawnWorker; if no slot is available it returns spawned=false.
name: SpawnFreeExploration

reason.description: Concrete reason for departing from the canonical frontier; name the orthogonal hypothesis, evidence, or expected information gain.

description: Return curator-owned executable leaf difficulties, pending checkpoint status, and the global_consolidation_directive. Dispatch targeted workers only against a returned leaf; launch a full-problem global attack only when that directive reports ready=true.
name: DifficultyFrontier

description: Record the evidence-backed outcome of one worker assigned to a canonical difficulty. This does not edit parent/child structure: only the curator does that at checkpoints. Use resolved only when the exact assigned difficulty is established, refuted only with a checkable counterexample, advanced for a genuine narrowed boundary, and unchanged otherwise.
name: RecordDifficultyOutcome

description:
Wait until one active worker finishes, or until the timeout is reached.

Use this tool to collect worker lifecycle results. If the maximum number of active workers has been reached, call TaskOutput before spawning more workers.

Return content is JSON. It always includes completed, active_count, active_worker_ids, active_workers, max_workers, and available_worker_slots. Completed workers may include a worker-local difficulty_handoff. It is evidence for the next checkpoint curator, not a permission to invent a new target immediately. Use DifficultyFrontier to read canonical executable leaves. RecordDifficultyOutcome only assesses the exact canonical difficulty assigned to a worker; parent/child structure is curator-owned. It may include timed_out when no worker finishes before the timeout; solved and solution_path when the original problem is solved; human_expert_updates when hint.md or knowledge/references changed during the run; and progress_audit with the independent process auditor's latest verdict and persisted checkpoint files.
name: TaskOutput

seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait before returning active worker status.

description: Returns the current date and time in ISO 8601 format.
name: GetCurrentTime
